Monday June 29 surged +5.56% (+$6,541) as MU Q3 FY2026 beat drove semiconductor complex and AMAT analyst target upgrades ($720–$790) lifted the stock to ~$650+. Tuesday June 30 added +2.59% (+$3,217) as PCE May 2026 data was absorbed without a rate-shock (outperformed SPY by +1.81% on PCE day). Portfolio peaked at $127,360.87 (June 30) — up +$9,755 / +8.27% intraweek. Then reversal: July 1 fell -4.92% (-$6,270) vs SPY -0.14% (-4.78% relative underperformance), and July 2 fell further -5.18% (-$7,050) vs SPY -0.13% (-5.05% underperformance). Semiconductor sector-driven selloff ahead of the July 4 holiday. Position count dropped from 6 to 4 on July 2 — FLEX (-2.92% as of July 1 12PM) closed per Friday rule, and one additional position closed (likely via stop-loss or partial trade plan execution). SMTC was absent from July 1 live snapshot (likely closed per June 29 trade plan). Final equity: $114,029.11 (July 2 close). Week net: -$3,776.67 / -3.21%. Portfolio +14.03% from $100K starting capital.

weekly_summary_2026_07_13.thesis: AI semiconductor sector under near-term profit-taking pressure from SK Hynix ADR post-IPO pullback (-10% on Nasdaq after record $26.5B debut Friday July 10) and Samsung Q2 sell-the-news. TSMC Q2 earnings Thursday July 16 expected to confirm AI demand 'extremely robust' ($39-40B guided, >30% FY2026 growth). Portfolio consolidates to 3 positions: AMAT (AI equipment anchor, +46%, TSMC earnings = direct catalyst), LLY (defensive GLP-1 healthcare, +20%, immune to chip selloff), AMD (new entry — Zen 6 Venice launch July 22, Advancing AI conference July 22-23, Q2 earnings Aug 4; Goldman $640 / Stifel $635). CPI June 2026 Tuesday July 14 is the primary macro risk.
